To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gel temperature during the electrophoresis of single‐stranded DNA fragments is the main factor determining the sensitivity of the SSCP analysis, that a change of the gel temperature by ±10°C from 20°C during SSCP electrophoresis increases the sensitivity of mutation and SNP detection by 2‐3 times, and that the MSSCP technology can detect more mutations in a given DNA fragment than SSCP analysis performed at a constant temperature.

the gel temperature during electrophoreses can be precisely controlled, that increasing the gel temperatures by 8°C from 23° C during SSCP analysis leads to the disappearance of electrophoretic mobility differences between all alleles, and that the MSSCP method is a useful tool for SNP screening and preselection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a method for the rapid detection of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the human genome.
the development of a new technology, MSSCP, which can be used for SNP and point mutation detection, and which can be applied to the analysis of large numbers of samples in the field of genomics.
the development of new technologies for the analysis of DNA sequences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MSSCP is a fast and reliable tool for the detection of single‐nucleotide mutations in PCR products.
the new MSSCP method is more sensitive and more reliable than classical SSCP and that it can detect SNPs that are undetectable by classical SSCP.
the MSSCP technique can be recommended as an alternative to classical SSCP for genotyping purposes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MSSCP technology is a fast, reliable and cost‐effective method for SNP and mutation detection.
the MSSCP method is a powerful technique for the detection of SNPs and mutations in DNA fragments of 100–500 bp in length.
the MSSCP technique is a very powerful and sensitive technique for mutation detection, especially when combined with other methods such as DNA sequencing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gel temperature during SSCP electrophoresis is a critical parameter for the detection of DNA polymorphism.
the MSSCP method allows the analysis of a large number of samples with a small amount of reagents.
MSSCP is a very useful tool for the detection and preselection of SNPs and point mutations, especially in large‐scale studies.
